idle.evidence: Portraits: AFTER rows show a mix of bandanas, headbands and varied head-cloths where BEFORE had mostly bare hair and the odd headband. At 40 studs the rose bindle and rucksack show on the backs of looks 2, 5, 8 and 10, and the pink bundle is also visible from the front on looks 2 and 8. The bandanas and headbands read, but the head-cloths are pale and low-contrast. The bundles are small and blend into the shirts. At 170 studs the pink and rose dabs are faintly visible but tiny, and at actual pixels the row is indistinguishable. Nothing resembles the hauler's large tan sack, the merchant's yellow pack, the builder's planks or the healer's bag, because the rose colour and small size are distinct.

farmer.evidence: AFTER portraits show black, gold, red-brown and dark-brown hair tufts under the hat brim, so the four looks now differ in hair colour and style. At 40 studs the tufts are small but visible; the front view shows slight hair colour at the sides. At 170 studs the straw hats dominate and there is no visible change. The hoe and hat read exactly as before.

builder.evidence: Black, gold, red and brown tufts or ponytails are clear under the teal cap in the portraits. At 40 studs, small tufts show beside the face on looks 1 and 3, and the orange locks on look 3 are noticeable from the front. From behind the plank stack still hides the hair. At 170 studs there is no visible change. The cap, mallet and planks read unchanged.

hauler.evidence: Portraits show black sideburn locks, gold curls and orange ponytails under the blue beret, so the looks differ in hair colour. At 40 studs the tufts are only faintly visible from the front. The sack on the back and the blue hat read as before. At 170 studs there is no change.

merchant.evidence: BEFORE portraits have the golden beam and pan crossing the chin and jaw, and the pole sits to the left. AFTER the head is clear and the beam is held low across the chest with a hanging pan, so the face is unobstructed. Hair tufts of black, gold, orange and brown add variation. At 40 studs the beam and pans read as a balance in front of the body and the plume is visible. At 170 studs the beam is a small gold smear mixed with the cast shadow, so the scale is only partly readable as a scale. It reads as a gold item, but BEFORE had a taller pole and plume that were a little more distinct from above.

healer.evidence: AFTER portraits show a green cross standing on the front-facing upper hood, above the brim, in addition to the flat green cross on top. It is clearly visible in all four looks. BEFORE showed only the flat green slab on top. At 40 studs the added cross is a small green mark on the hat but it does read and sits beside the staff. At 170 studs there is no visible difference from BEFORE. The white hood and staff still read as healer.

regressions: Merchant at 170 studs: the lowered, low-contrast scale beam merges with its shadow and is slightly less distinct than the tall pole and plume BEFORE.

Idle: the pale head-cloths and the small rose bundles are low-contrast against the cream shirts. Some looks, such as 3, 4 and 6, show no new accessory, so about five of the ten still read as accessory-free.
notes: Hair tufts lift portrait variation on all four hat jobs, but at 40 studs they are marginal and at 170 studs invisible, so variation stays below the pass mark of 4 for those sheets. The idle accessories add some variety, but they are small and low-contrast beyond close range. The healer cross and the merchant scale fix both work in the portrait, with a minor loss of scale clarity at the aerial camera.
